PUMP (2007) by DAVID ADEY. David Adey transforms an ordinary football into a strange kinetic sculpture. Its surface is densely covered with drywall screws, while a hidden respirator repeatedly inflates and deflates the ball, producing a slow, mechanical rhythm. Created in 2007, Pump was later included in the 2010 California Biennial at the Orange County Museum of Art. #art #avantgarde #niche #artist #weird

Vadim Gordeev is a Barcelona-based performance artist, engineer, and illusion designer who transforms simple mechanical systems into mesmerizing living sculptures. Blending engineering, kinetic art, magic, and performance, he creates poetic illusions where everyday objects appear to move, breathe, and defy logic. His work explores the fragile boundary between science and imagination, turning precision mechanics into unforgettable visual experiences. #weird #artist #art #avantgarde #niche

Artist Casey Curran creates kinetic sculptures that combine mechanical systems with forms inspired by plants and natural structures. In this prototype, layers of delicate petals are connected so that a single mechanical action produces a rippling movement across the entire structure. Instead of every element moving independently, the motion travels through the sculpture like a wave. This type of movement is central to Curran’s practice. Using motors, wires, cranks and carefully engineered mechanisms, he creates artificial flowers and organisms that bloom, flutter and contract.  The machinery is artificial, but the movement feels strangely organic ,engineering becomes a way of imitating the rhythms of living systems. #art #artist #fashion #avantgarde #design

Thomas D. Westergaard is a Danish designer and founder of Ceremoni Studio, where he transforms the traditional candle into a kinetic sculpture. Instead of treating wax as a static object, he engineers candles that bend, twist, and weave together as they burn. Every prototype is tested through long time-lapse recordings to study the flame, the melting wax, and the structure, refining each design until movement and combustion become one. His work sits somewhere between industrial design, engineering, and performance. #art #artist #avantgarde #candles #timelapse

Every friend group has that one person who thinks they're in charge. Apparently the Squirtle Squad is no exception. For this satisfying Pokémon sand art ASMR video, I recreated a group of six Squirtles using colored sand. Five of them are just being their adorable little selves, smiling, waving, and looking like they're having the best day ever. Then there's the shiny Squirtle in the middle. Black sunglasses. Arms crossed. Absolutely zero interest in participating in whatever the other five are doing. He's clearly the main character, and he knows it. The whole design reminds me of the original Squirtle Squad from the Pokémon anime, where a group of mischievous Squirtles became memorable partly because of their sunglasses and attitude. Giving the center Squirtle that same energy completely changes the personality of the artwork. What makes this particular sand art project interesting is how much variation you can get from the same Pokémon design. Every Squirtle shares the recognizable blue body, cream-colored belly, brown shell, big red eyes, and curled tail, but the different poses and facial expressions make each one feel unique. The center shiny Squirtle also has a slightly different attitude thanks to the black-and-white pixel-style sunglasses and crossed arms, which immediately separate him from the rest of the group. Recreating six Pokémon in one colored sand art piece also means a lot of repetitive sections. Blue sand fills the bodies, lighter tones create the shells and bellies, pink sand adds the mouths, and the darker colors bring out the outlines and facial details. That repetition is part of what makes the process so satisfying to watch. Each section gradually builds another character until the entire group comes together. It's a mix of Pokémon nostalgia, Squirtle Squad fan art, satisfying sand painting, colorful character art, handmade Pokémon crafts, and relaxing ASMR.
